# Foundations Assignment Instructions, Paste-Ready

**Generated by `tools/build-canvas-assignments.js`. Do not hand-edit.**
The `Success criteria` list at the bottom of every body is lifted verbatim from
that day's `successCriteria` array in `foundations/foundations-*-data.js`.
Change a criterion in the data file and rerun the generator; never edit one in
Canvas, and never edit one here.

The student-facing framing, the module bullets, the checkpoint wording, and the
F5 reflection questions, is hand-written in the `DAYS` table inside the
generator, because the data file's prompts are addressed to the teacher. Edit it
there, then rerun.

```bash
node tools/build-canvas-assignments.js          # write
node tools/build-canvas-assignments.js --check  # fail on drift, write nothing
```

## How to paste one of these

1. Canvas, **Assignments**, then the assignment named in the heading below, or
   **+ Assignment** if it does not exist yet.
2. Name it exactly as given. That name has to match PowerSchool character for
   character; see Section 2 of `CANVAS-BUILD-GUIDE.md`.
3. In the Rich Content Editor, click the **`</>`** icon to open the HTML editor.
   **Never paste this into the visual editor.** Pasting rendered HTML there
   injects wrapper `<div>`s and inline font declarations.
4. Paste the whole block.
5. Set the assignment options from the table under each heading, and set due
   dates **per section** using the **+Add** row in *Assign To*. ZCHS runs an
   alternating Green/Silver block schedule, so "the beginning of our next class
   period" is a different calendar date for each section. One blanket due date
   marks two or three sections late through no fault of their own.
6. Save, then build the calendar event for that day from
   `foundations-calendar-events.md` and insert this assignment into its
   ASSIGNMENT row through the course-links panel.

Every link points at the live GitHub Pages build:
`https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/ap-world-history/foundations/`

## The submission path these bodies describe

Verified against `foundations/foundations-topic-renderer.js`. Students complete
every module on the live site, then use the **Save Your Work** panel below the
module cards: **Gather All My Work**, then **Copy to Clipboard**, then paste into
the Canvas Text Entry box. There is nothing to download and no second capture
channel: no draft box on any Foundations page carries any other submit control.
See `FORM-REMOVAL-FINDINGS.md` for the audit behind that statement.

## F1 - Geo Shapes Civilization

**Assignment name (Canvas and PowerSchool, identical):** `F1 - Geo Shapes Civilization`  
**Points:** 20  |  **Submission type:** Online, Text Entry  |  **Attempts:** Unlimited  |  **Assignment group:** Foundations  
**Source data file:** `foundations/foundations-1-geography-data.js`  
**Lesson page:** `foundations/foundations-1-geography.html`

```html
<h2>Foundations 1: Geography Shapes Civilization</h2>
<p><em>How did geography drive the shift from hunter-gatherer bands to the first civilizations?</em></p>
<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the lesson</h3>
<p><a href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/ap-world-history/foundations/foundations-1-geography.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Foundations 1 - Geography Shapes Civilization</a></p>
<p>Everything happens on the website. There is nothing to download.</p>
<h3>Step 2 &mdash; Complete every module</h3>
<p>Work top to bottom and complete all of them. Read the three Learning Targets and the Success Criteria before you start.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Map &amp; Geography Check</strong> &mdash; locate the four great river valleys, the Fertile Crescent, and the grasslands. Predict where agriculture begins and why.</li>
<li><strong>First &amp; 10</strong> &mdash; the Neolithic Revolution. Mark one geographic advantage, one consequence of surplus, and one cost of switching to farming.</li>
<li><strong>Content Delivery</strong> &mdash; all lecture cards.</li>
<li><strong>BeSurreal</strong></li>
<li><strong>AP Skill Builder: Contextualization</strong></li>
<li><strong>Checkpoint 1</strong></li>
<li><strong>Evidence Lab</strong></li>
<li><strong>Socrates AI Coach</strong></li>
<li><strong>Checkpoint 2</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Type a real response in every box.</strong> Gather All My Work collects exactly what you typed and nothing else. An empty box is an empty box in your submission, and it is the only record I see.</p>
<h3>Step 3 &mdash; The Checkpoint</h3>
<p>Explain how geography made the shift from hunting and gathering to civilization possible. Identify a specific geographic condition, connect it to the beginning of agriculture, and explain how the resulting surplus produced at least one characteristic of civilization. Use cause-and-effect reasoning.</p>
<h3>Step 4 &mdash; Submit in Canvas</h3>
<ol>
<li>Scroll to the <strong>Save Your Work</strong> panel below the module cards.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Gather All My Work</strong>. This pulls every response you typed today into one block.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Copy to Clipboard</strong>.</li>
<li>Paste everything into the submission box below and click Submit.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>This is the only way your work reaches me.</strong> BeHistorical saves your typing in the browser on the device you used, but that is not a submission and it does not follow you to another Chromebook. If you do not submit in Canvas, I have no record that you did the work.</p>
<h3>Due</h3>
<p>The beginning of our next AP World History class period.</p>
<h3>Success criteria</h3>
<ol>
<li>I can describe how hunter-forager life differed from settled agricultural life, and name a specific geographic feature, a river, fertile soil, a domesticable species, that made the beginning of agriculture possible.</li>
<li>I can trace the causal chain from agricultural surplus to at least three characteristics of civilization.</li>
<li>I can write a contextualization sentence that identifies a geographic condition and explains how it shaped the shift to farming or the rise of a civilization.</li>
</ol>
```

## F2 - Belief Systems

**Assignment name (Canvas and PowerSchool, identical):** `F2 - Belief Systems`  
**Points:** 20  |  **Submission type:** Online, Text Entry  |  **Attempts:** Unlimited  |  **Assignment group:** Foundations

**Lesson page:** `foundations/foundations-2-belief-systems.html`

```html
<h2>Foundations 2: Belief Systems and Cultural Exchange</h2>
<p><em>How did six major belief systems, Confucianism, Daoism, Hinduism, Buddhism, Christianity, and Islam, shape societies and spread across the world?</em></p>
<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the lesson</h3>
<p><a href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/ap-world-history/foundations/foundations-2-belief-systems.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Foundations 2 - Belief Systems and Cultural Exchange</a></p>

<p>Work top to bottom and complete all of them. Read the three Learning Targets and the Success Criteria before you start.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Map &amp; Geography Check</strong> &mdash; trace how Buddhism spread from India across Asia. Identify the routes it followed and the mechanism behind each, trade, state adoption, or missionaries, and treat it as the model for how all six systems moved.</li>
<li><strong>First &amp; 10</strong> &mdash; six belief systems in one survey. Mark the core idea of each, and one example of syncretism, a belief system changing as it entered a new region.</li>
<li><strong>Content Delivery</strong> &mdash; all lecture cards.</li>
<li><strong>BeSurreal</strong></li>
<li><strong>AP Skill Builder: Comparison</strong></li>
<li><strong>Checkpoint 1</strong></li>
<li><strong>Evidence Lab</strong></li>
<li><strong>Socrates AI Coach</strong></li>
<li><strong>Checkpoint 2</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Type a real response in every box.</strong> Gather All My Work collects exactly what you typed and nothing else. An empty box is an empty box in your submission, and it is the only record I see.</p>
<h3>Step 3 &mdash; The Checkpoint</h3>
<p>Choose ONE of the six belief systems and explain how it functioned as a social institution in a specific region before c.1200. Name the belief system, identify a specific institutional function it performed, and support the claim with historical evidence.</p>
<h3>Step 4 &mdash; Submit in Canvas</h3>
<ol>
<li>Scroll to the <strong>Save Your Work</strong> panel below the module cards.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Gather All My Work</strong>. This pulls every response you typed today into one block.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Copy to Clipboard</strong>.</li>
<li>Paste everything into the submission box below and click Submit.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>This is the only way your work reaches me.</strong> BeHistorical saves your typing in the browser on the device you used, but that is not a submission and it does not follow you to another Chromebook. If you do not submit in Canvas, I have no record that you did the work.</p>
<h3>Due</h3>
<p>The beginning of our next AP World History class period.</p>
<h3>Success criteria</h3>
<ol>
<li>I can state the central idea of each of the six belief systems and where it originated.</li>
<li>I can identify a specific institutional function of a belief system, education, law, welfare, legitimacy, social order, and give a concrete historical example.</li>
<li>I can explain at least one mechanism by which a belief system spread, trade route, state adoption, missionary, civil service exam, or monastic network, and give a specific example of syncretism that shows how belief systems change as they travel.</li>
</ol>
```

## F5 - World at c.1200 SAQ

**Assignment name (Canvas and PowerSchool, identical):** `F5 - World at c.1200 SAQ`  
**Points:** 30  |  **Submission type:** Online, Text Entry  |  **Attempts:** Unlimited  |  **Assignment group:** Foundations  
**Source data file:** `foundations/foundations-5-world-at-1200-data.js`  
**Lesson page:** `foundations/foundations-5-world-at-1200.html`

```html
<h2>Foundations 5: The World at c.1200</h2>
<p><em>What does the world look like at c.1200, and how do historians explain it?</em></p>
<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the lesson</h3>
<p><a href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/ap-world-history/foundations/foundations-5-world-at-1200.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Foundations 5 - The World at c.1200</a></p>
<p>Everything happens on the website. There is nothing to download.</p>
<h3>Step 2 &mdash; Complete every module</h3>
<p>Work top to bottom and complete all of them. Read the three Learning Targets and the Success Criteria before you start.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Map &amp; Geography Check</strong> &mdash; place the six AP World regions on the map, attach one fact from Foundations 1 through 4 to each, and locate the trade networks connecting them.</li>
<li><strong>First &amp; 10</strong> &mdash; six windows on c.1200. For each regional snapshot, mark which Foundations theme, geography, belief systems, states and power, or trade networks, best explains it.</li>
<li><strong>Content Delivery</strong> &mdash; all lecture cards.</li>
<li><strong>BeSurreal</strong></li>
<li><strong>AP Skill Builder: The Five Historical Thinking Skills</strong></li>
<li><strong>Checkpoint 1</strong></li>
<li><strong>Evidence Lab</strong></li>
<li><strong>Socrates AI Coach</strong></li>
<li><strong>Checkpoint 2</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Type a real response in every box.</strong> Gather All My Work collects exactly what you typed and nothing else. An empty box is an empty box in your submission, and it is the only record I see.</p>
<h3>What an SAQ is</h3>
<p>A Short Answer Question is not an essay. It is one tight paragraph that does three things and stops: it makes a <strong>claim</strong> that answers the prompt directly, it supplies <strong>specific evidence</strong>, a named institution, person, place, date, or practice, and it supplies <strong>reasoning</strong> that explains why that evidence proves the claim. No introduction. No conclusion. No restating the prompt.</p>
<p><strong>Draft it yourself first.</strong> Write your full response before you open the Socrates AI Coach. The Coach is a revision tool, not a drafting tool, and a paragraph it wrote for you tells me nothing about what you can do in May, when you will be writing this by hand with no coach in the room. Write it badly if you have to. Then use Socrates to make it sharper.</p>
<h3>Step 3 &mdash; The Checkpoint</h3>
<p>This is your first complete AP-style SAQ. Respond to this prompt using everything from the Foundations unit: <em>Explain how the historical conditions that developed before c.1200 shaped the world that AP World History begins studying.</em> Your response needs a defensible claim, specific evidence from at least two Foundations days, and explicit reasoning that connects your evidence to your claim.</p>
<h3>Step 4 &mdash; Reflect before you submit</h3>
<p>Answer these three in the Checkpoint 2 box, under your SAQ. They close out the Foundations unit.</p>
<ol>
<li>Which of the five AP historical thinking skills do you feel most ready to use in Unit 1, and what in the Foundations unit made you feel ready?</li>
<li>Which part of your SAQ still feels weakest, the claim, the evidence, or the reasoning, and what would you need in order to fix it?</li>
<li>Which Foundations theme, geography, belief systems, states and power, or trade networks, does your argument depend on most? Name it. That is your contextualization.</li>
</ol>
<h3>Step 5 &mdash; Submit in Canvas</h3>
<ol>
<li>Scroll to the <strong>Save Your Work</strong> panel below the module cards.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Gather All My Work</strong>. This pulls every response you typed today into one block.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Copy to Clipboard</strong>.</li>
<li>Paste everything into the submission box below and click Submit.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>This is the only way your work reaches me.</strong> BeHistorical saves your typing in the browser on the device you used, but that is not a submission and it does not follow you to another Chromebook. If you do not submit in Canvas, I have no record that you did the work.</p>
<h3>Due</h3>
<p>The beginning of our next AP World History class period.</p>
<h3>Success criteria</h3>
<ol>
<li>I can write one specific sentence about each of the six AP World regions at c.1200 that names a specific feature, institution, trade connection, or belief system, and explain which Foundations theme mattered most, using evidence from at least two days.</li>
<li>I can explain each AP historical thinking skill in my own words and identify where it appeared in Foundations Days 1–4.</li>
<li>I can write an SAQ paragraph with a defensible claim in the first sentence, at least two specific pieces of historical evidence, and a reasoning sentence that explains the connection.</li>
</ol>
```

## F0 has no assignment body

`F0 - Intro to BeHistorical` is a real assignment in the module structure and it
appears in `foundations-calendar-events.md`, but its Canvas description has not
been authored. Nothing in this file covers it, and nothing here should be adapted
into it by hand: F0 is the only Foundations day whose checkpoint is a Historian's
Pledge rather than a content response, and its module bullets, framing, and
grading weight, 10 points against the 20 that F1 through F4 carry, all differ.

When it is written, add an `F0` entry to the `DAYS` table in
`tools/build-canvas-assignments.js` and rerun, so its success criteria stay
bound to `foundations/foundations-0-intro-to-behistorical-data.js` the same way
the other five are.
